title: Three kinds of people
hookLine: three ways people deal with an attachment

cards: Three people have each come into a large sum of money. Not stolen. Not quite clean either: they got it, Ignatius says, not purely for the love of God.
And now each one feels the weight of it. Not the money itself, the grip it has on them. All three want to be at peace with God and rid of that grip.
They even agree on the goal. What separates them is what they actually do next. Ignatius sets them side by side in the second week and lets the one praying watch.

teach.b: The first person wants to be free of the attachment. Really wants it. But never takes the means.
Next month. After this busy stretch. Ignatius says they put it off right up to the hour of death.
The second person also wants to be free, but on one condition: keeping the money. They'd like God to come around to what they've already decided. They'll pray about it, as long as the answer is yes.
The third person wants to be free in a different way. They don't cling to keeping it, and they don't cling to giving it up.

teach.h: THE SECOND: ONLY IF I KEEP IT.
teach.b: They want to keep it or let it go only as God moves them and as serves God better. And while they wait to see which, they live as if they'd already let it go in their heart. That person might keep the money.
The meditation isn't about the money. It's about who holds whom. Jesus puts it in one line, in Matthew's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims: "For where thy treasure is, there is thy heart also."
Ignatius adds an honest note: if you feel a pull against letting go, ask in prayer for exactly the thing you resist, even against your own inclination.

teach.h: THE THIRD: AS GOD MOVES ME.
teach.b: He doesn't pretend the third way is easy.
The meditation ends with the same three conversations as yesterday's.

teach.h: WHERE THY TREASURE IS, THERE IS THY HEART.
teach.b: And it isn't only about money: a phone, a grudge, a role at work that has become who you are.

how: In the second week of an Ignatian retreat, people pray the meditation on the three classes of people after the two standards, using it to test how free they are before making a choice.

games.q: what does “three kinds of people” mean?
o: Ignatius's three ways of facing an attachment
three groups of pilgrims on the road to Rome
three steps for paying back stolen money

games.q: three kinds of people — tap the pairs.
p: wants God to come to their terms
keep it or not, as God moves

s: the third kind of person must give the money away
they may keep it or not. what decides is God's service, not the grip.
the second kind wants God to come around to what they already want
they want to be free of the attachment, but only if they keep the thing.
the first kind never wants to change
they do want to. they just never take the means, right up to the hour of death.

games.q: you've come into money you're too attached to, and you want to be free of the grip. which way does Ignatius hold up?
o: mean to deal with it later.
keep the money and ask God to bless the plan.
want only what serves God, keep it or not.
games.why: the third way. the surprise: that person might keep the money. the meditation is about the grip, not the sum.

practice: Bring to mind one attachment, something you own, a role, a habit, a plan you've already settled, and ask honestly which of the three you are with it: someday, bargaining, or free. No grade.
For this sit, try the third way: hold it with an open hand, neither clutching it nor throwing it away. If you pray, ask God to move you whichever way serves.

wordCard.voice: Three kinds of people. One puts it off, one bargains, and one wants only what serves God, keep it or not. Today's word.

orig.note: Spanish: Ignatius's own heading for the three kinds of people, rendered in English as three classes or three pairs.

carryVoice: Your line: really free. One says someday, one bargains, one opens the hand and waits. Rest well.

sources.q: For where thy treasure is, there is thy heart also.

sources.ref: Spiritual Exercises, three classes of men (no. 149–157)
